Edited by Chieko Yamano.

Michaelmas 2008, Oxford. Eight manuscripts were utilized, though the commentary was not. A = Matsunami 404, CE 1595.

Now I shall describe another supreme method for the practice of elixirs (rasāyana).
By the mere knowledge of which, the characteristic of the body and its means [is understood]. || 1 ||
Soma, sihlaka, kastūrī, bhaiṣajya, and yellow sandalwood—whether used individually or combined together—these are the deceivers of old age and death. || 2 ||
The best [type of recipient] is one born of the five noble families; the middling is one born of one's own kin; the inferior is one born of common women. An elder should avoid a youth. || 3 ||
She who is dark-complexioned with beautiful limbs, who is in her menses during the dark fortnight,
a young girl with glossy hair, fragrant, and having dark pupils— (4).
Its flower is highly praised as it grants the accomplishment of all desired goals; however,
that which blooms during the bright fortnight (śuklapakṣa) is not auspicious, as it causes old age and other such ailments.
Free from the first and last [impurities], pure, and resembling clear crystal, the musk of the deer is praised; its collection as kastūrī is auspicious.
The excellent essence of the Hatya [flower], the supreme collection of medicines produced from milk and other foods, is gathered together with yellow sandalwood. (7)
Clarified butter (ghṛta) is of three kinds: that produced from the head, that produced from the stalk (nalikā), and that produced from the flesh.
The clarified butter from the head is the best; that which originates from the stalk is middling.
This lowest [substance], produced from flesh, is the most excellent elixir according to the prescribed method.
Candana promotes the nourishment of the body; turuṣka is a protector against all [evils];
mṛganābhi destroys diseases; and bhaiṣajya brings about peace. One should always employ catuḥsama at dawn and use it constantly.
When the Moon is moving, it should be drunk during the Moon's movement;
when the Protector is the Moon, the Sun should be drunk by means of the Sun, for the Sun flows within the Teacher.
Having prepared this substance, one should administer it as a nasal drop constantly;
by practicing this yoga for six months, one's lifespan always increases. (11)
By means of the perfectly pure act of giving a dwarf’s measure of land,
one shall live free from all disease, like the moon in its bright fortnight.
The water there is stainless, yellowish-green, free from impurities and dirt, pure, and devoid of the four defects. || 13 ||
Transparent, stainless, clear, and somewhat resembling crystal—thus indeed is pure crystal; such is the supreme *piṇḍabandhana*. 14.
Avoiding meat, liquor, and sexual intercourse, the wise and disciplined man should protect his own body in seclusion. (15)
One should cause the devoted disciple, properly prepared, to enter the interior of the cave; there,
the propitiation of the deity must be performed, accompanied by offerings and oblations.

Through the yoga of one's own tutelary deity, having performed the uninterrupted recitation of the mantra and the meritorious act of giving, one should cause the disciple to feel satisfaction. || 17 ||
Having attained a place free from wind, remaining unobstructed, and having assumed a comfortable posture, the wise man should maintain silence. (18)
One should thoroughly purify one's own body for a period of seven days;
thereafter, one may practice the ritual for ten years and so forth.
And for two years, the wise one should always protect [the practice] at the time of accomplishment;
when twelve years have passed, he becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair.
Freed from various diseases, he shall live as long as the moon and stars;
he becomes beloved by gods, asuras, humans, and women. (21)
One should always consume the five substances as a constant awakening;
this rite being complete, the fulfillment of one's desires proceeds.
One’s body becomes equal to the wish-fulfilling cow (kāmadhenu), and one attains the siddhi of the Khecarī. || 22 ||
In this [rite], one should use the charcoal, brick-dust, and *nirguṇḍī* of the Buddha, along with fragrant substances, the sap of *dhuttūra* leaves, musk, and sandalwood. || 23 ||
He who rubs his own body with [the powder] mixed with *coravāla* becomes free from all diseases, devoid of poison, and endowed with splendor. || 24 ||
He who drinks for a year the powder produced from triphalā and sandalwood, together with śitalā, musk, shall become free from old age and disease.
One should consume the powder of triphalā and candana together with musk;
by using this for only six months, one will become long-lived and possessed of beauty. (26)
He who constantly drinks this cool water, mixed with musk and the three myrobalans (triphalā) and kept in a stone vessel, shall become free from old age and disease.
If a person consumes *candana* derived from the three decoctions for six months, whatever accomplishment (*siddhi*) arises for him is desired; there is no doubt in this matter. (28)
Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, on the procedure for elixirs (rasāyana).
